cases.translation: The wind was pushing the rusty carousels, slowly turning them.
cases.explain: «Ветер» is the grammatical subject of «толкал» (was pushing), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Ей эту тарелку отец подарил, а до конца ___ день.
cases.translation: Her father had given her that flying disc, and there was only a day left until the end of the shift.
cases.explain: The preposition «до» (until) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Еще раз, окинув взгляду в сцену, пошел к ___ из театра.
cases.translation: Once more glancing at the stage, he walked toward the exit from the theater.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» (toward) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Юра наклонился, сорвал ___, покрутил в пальцах и, горько усмехнувшись, подул на него.
cases.translation: Yura bent down, plucked the flower, twirled it in his fingers, and, smiling bitterly, blew on it.
cases.explain: «Цветок» is the direct object of the transitive verb «сорвал» (plucked), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Так вот, под ___ тьмы, безлунной ночью, вынес сундук и где-то закопал, отметив место клада на карте.
cases.translation: So then, under cover of darkness, on a moonless night, he carried out the chest and buried it somewhere, marking the treasure's spot on a map.
cases.explain: The preposition «под» (under, static position) governs the instrumental case.

cases.translation: He lay down in the darkness.
cases.explain: «В» expressing static location governs the prepositional case.

reading.ru: Болезненная тоска и ностальгия пронимали его до глубины души, особенно здесь, в этих стенах.
reading.question: What feeling gripped Yura especially strongly inside these walls?
reading.correct: Painful longing and nostalgia
reading.explain: The text says painful longing and nostalgia pierced him to the depths of his soul, especially here.

reading.ru: Большинство лежало грудами гнилых мокрых досок, на которых ещё виднелись остатки старой краски.
reading.question: What condition were most of the children's cabins in?
options: Piles of rotten, wet boards with traces of old paint
reading.correct: Piles of rotten, wet boards with traces of old paint
reading.explain: The text says most lay in piles of rotten, wet boards still showing traces of old paint.

reading.ru: Более или менее уцелевшими оказались всего два домика.
reading.question: How many of the cabins had survived more or less intact?
reading.correct: Two
reading.explain: The text states that only two little houses turned out to be more or less intact.

reading.ru: Вот только детей тут уже давно не было, и площадка заросла высоченной травой.
reading.question: What had happened to the playground since children stopped coming?
options: It became overgrown with tall grass
It was turned into a parking lot
reading.correct: It became overgrown with tall grass
reading.explain: The text says there had long been no children here, and the playground had grown over with tall grass.

reading.ru: Не понимая, зачем он это делает, и даже не задавая себе такого вопроса, Юра уселся на сиденье и слегка оттолкнулся ногами.
reading.question: What did Yura do at the old carousel, without knowing why?
options: He sat on the seat and pushed off gently with his feet
reading.correct: He sat on the seat and pushed off gently with his feet
reading.explain: Without understanding why, Yura sat on the seat and gave a gentle push off with his feet.

reading.ru: Вдруг в ночных шорохах послышались чьи-то тихие шаги и скрип половиц крыльца.
reading.question: What alerted Yurka to someone else's presence at night?
options: Quiet footsteps and creaking porch floorboards
reading.correct: Quiet footsteps and creaking porch floorboards
reading.explain: Amid the night sounds, quiet footsteps and the creak of porch floorboards suddenly became audible.

reading.ru: Саша втянул голову в плечи и что-то запищал, обслюнявив Юрке ладонь.
reading.question: How did the boy Sasha initially react when caught?
options: He hunched his shoulders and squeaked, slobbering on Yurka's hand
reading.correct: He hunched his shoulders and squeaked, slobbering on Yurka's hand
reading.explain: Sasha hunched his shoulders and squeaked something, drooling on Yurka's palm.

reading.ru: «Я просто, просто хотел смородины», – залепетал малец.
reading.question: What did the little boy claim he only wanted?
reading.correct: Currants (смородина)
reading.explain: The boy stammers that he just wanted some currants.

reading.ru: «Разве двери не запирают?
reading.question: What does Sasha ask, explaining how he got out of the cabin?
reading.correct: Whether the doors are locked
reading.explain: Sasha asks whether the doors aren't locked, explaining how he slipped out.

reading.ru: В тот момент, когда Юрка тихонько открыл дверь спальни, Володя стоял в свете тусклого ночника над пустой кроватью и смотрел перед собой круглыми от ужаса глазами.
reading.question: What did Yurka see when he quietly opened the bedroom door?
options: Volodya standing over an empty bed with eyes wide with horror
reading.correct: Volodya standing over an empty bed with eyes wide with horror
reading.explain: Volodya was standing in the dim nightlight over an empty bed, staring ahead with eyes round with horror.

reading.ru: Малышня больше не шепталась.
reading.question: What happened to the little kids' whispering once the ghost story began?
options: It stopped — they listened intently to Olezhka instead
reading.correct: It stopped — they listened intently to Olezhka instead
reading.explain: The text says the little ones stopped whispering, listening tensely to Olezhka instead.

reading.ru: Давным-давно, еще до Великой Октябрьской революции, неподалеку стояло барское поместье, а в нем жили молодые граф с графиней.
reading.question: When and where was Yurka's ghost story set?
options: Long ago, before the October Revolution, in a nearby manor house
In modern times, in the camp itself
reading.correct: Long ago, before the October Revolution, in a nearby manor house
reading.explain: The story begins long ago, before the Great October Revolution, in a nearby manor where a young count and countess lived.

reading.ru: Он подарил своей графине на память красивую алмазную брошь и ушёл воевать, но так и не вернулся.
reading.question: What did the count give the countess before leaving for war?
reading.correct: A beautiful diamond brooch
reading.explain: He gave his countess a beautiful diamond brooch as a keepsake before going to war, from which he never returned.

reading.ru: Говорят, что хоронили её всё в том же чёрном вдовьем платье, а вот брошь в могилу не положили.
reading.question: What was NOT buried with the countess?
reading.correct: The brooch
reading.explain: The text says she was buried in the same black widow's dress, but the brooch was not put in the grave.

reading.ru: То мебель двигалась сама собой, то двери открывались.
reading.question: What strange occurrences began at the manor after the brooch disappeared?
options: Furniture moved by itself and doors opened
reading.correct: Furniture moved by itself and doors opened
reading.explain: The text says furniture would move by itself, and doors would open on their own.

reading.ru: Мертвец этот, вожатый, совсем молодой, первый год в лагере.
reading.question: Who was the dead man in Yurka's story?
options: A young counselor in his first year at the camp
reading.correct: A young counselor in his first year at the camp
reading.explain: The text identifies the dead man as a counselor, very young, in his first year at the camp.

reading.ru: На следующее утро его нашли мёртвым.
reading.question: What happened to the counselor in the story the morning after he investigated the sounds?
options: He was found injured but alive
reading.correct: He was found dead
reading.explain: The next morning he was found dead.

reading.ru: Володя с Юркой переглянулись.
reading.question: What did Volodya and Yurka do after the ghost story frightened the children?
options: They exchanged glances and decided to stay with the children
They left immediately for the disco
reading.correct: They exchanged glances and decided to stay with the children
reading.explain: Volodya and Yurka exchanged glances, both realizing they should not leave the children alone now.

reading.ru: А Володя красивый, подумалось Юрке.
reading.question: What did Yurka think about Volodya while sitting in the dark room?
reading.correct: That Volodya was handsome
reading.explain: The text records Yurka's thought that Volodya was handsome.

reading.ru: «Я же просил не перебарщивать!»
reading.question: What did Volodya scold Yurka for after leaving the children's room?
reading.correct: Overdoing the scary story
reading.explain: Volodya reproaches Yurka, "I asked you not to overdo it!", referring to the frightening story.

reading.ru: Пугачёва дуэтом с Кузьминым пела о том, что в небе весеннем падали две звезды.
reading.question: What song drifted over from the disco while Yura and Volodya sat outside?
options: A Pugacheva and Kuzmin duet about two falling stars
reading.correct: A Pugacheva and Kuzmin duet about two falling stars
reading.explain: The text names a Pugacheva and Kuzmin duet about two stars falling in the spring sky.

reading.ru: Я вожатый, а они пионерки.
reading.question: What reason does Volodya give for not being interested in the girls chasing him?
options: He is a counselor and they are pioneers (campers)
reading.correct: He is a counselor and they are pioneers (campers)
reading.explain: Volodya explains simply, "I'm a counselor, and they are pioneers," implying it would be inappropriate.

reading.ru: На самом деле я помогал, доставал летающую тарелку.
reading.question: What was Yura actually doing on the roof, according to his explanation to Volodya?
options: Retrieving a girl's flying disc that got stuck up there
reading.correct: Retrieving a girl's flying disc that got stuck up there
reading.explain: Yura explains that he was actually helping retrieve a flying disc toy that had landed on the roof.

reading.ru: Полез в правый, вынул ручку и свёрнутую трубочкой тетрадку.
reading.question: What did Volodya take out of his right pocket to write down the new story idea?
options: A pen and a notebook rolled into a tube
reading.correct: A pen and a notebook rolled into a tube
reading.explain: Volodya reaches into his right pocket and pulls out a pen and a notebook rolled up like a tube.

reading.ru: В тот вечер на дискотеку Юрка так и не явился.
reading.question: Did Yurka end up going to the disco that evening?
options: Yes, and he danced all night
reading.correct: No, he never showed up
reading.explain: The text states plainly that Yurka never did show up at the disco that evening.

highlight.question: Which sentences contrast the camp buildings' former beauty with their current state of decay?
sentences: Чудом уцелевшая асфальтированная дорожка вывела его к детским отрядам.
Когда-то красивые, выкрашенные яркими красками и расписными узорами корпуса были похожи на домики из русских сказок.
Но теперь они выглядели плачевно: большинство лежало грудами гнилых мокрых досок, на которых ещё виднелись остатки старой краски.

Более или менее уцелевшими оказались всего два домика, — Юра уже не мог вспомнить их номеров, — у одного обвалилась левая стена и крыша, а другой остался почти невредимым, только немного просел и покосился.
Но заглядывать внутрь определённо не стоило: на крыльце провалился пол, входная дверь выпала, и проход зиял тёмным устрашающим провалом.
В этих корпусах всегда селили младшие отряды — подальше от дискотеки и кинозала.
Юра тоже жил здесь в одну из своих первых смен.
highlight.explain: These sentences describe how the colorfully painted buildings once resembled fairy tale houses but now lie in ruins with only old paint traces remaining.

highlight.question: Which sentence shows that the children were paying attention to Olezhka instead of the adults?
sentences: Юрка покрутил головой, всматриваясь в ровные ряды кроватей.
Малышня больше не шепталась.
Все напряжённо и внимательно слушали не взрослых, а взъерошенного картавого Олежку, который вещал загробным голосом:
highlight.explain: This sentence indicates that all the children were listening intently to Olezhka's story told in a sepulchral voice rather than to grown-ups.

highlight.question: Which sentences recount the tragic decline and death of the countess after her husband's death?
sentences: Она больше не носила красивых платьев и украшений, ходила вся в чёрном, но алмазную брошь — последний подарок мужа — постоянно держала рядом, то прикалывала к груди, то к волосам.
Время шло, графиня тосковала и вскоре заболела.
Она не хотела видеть никого, даже врача, и спустя год умерла.
Говорят, что хоронили её всё в том же чёрном вдовьем платье, а вот брошь в могилу не положили.
Брошь пропала!
highlight.explain: These sentences trace her mourning, illness, refusal to see anyone, and eventual death while wearing her widow's dress.

highlight.question: Which sentence shows Volodya and Yurka deciding they should remain with the children rather than leave?
sentences: Володя с Юркой переглянулись.
Не стоило сейчас уходить от детей — это было ясно обоим, и они расселись по углам.
Сидели молча: Володя — возле окна, а Юрка — возле двери, скучали.
highlight.explain: This sentence explains that they understood it was not the right time to leave and therefore settled themselves in the corners to stay.

highlight.question: Which sentence reveals Volodya's personal dislike of discos?
sentences: — оживился Володя.
— Ты что, на меня рассчитывал?
Но мы же не договаривались, да и вообще я не люблю дискотеки.
— он нахмурился и вдруг встрепенулся, что-то вспомнив.
— Меня сегодня уже приглашали.
highlight.explain: This sentence states his clear lack of interest in attending discos.

highlight.question: Which sentence expresses complaint about the counselors catching people at bad moments and drawing wrong conclusions?
sentences: — Я тут ни при чём.
Просто этих дурацких вожатых так и тянет застукивать в самый неподходящий момент, а потом, меня не слушая, делать какие-то свои выводы.
Ты про крышу, например, слышал?
highlight.explain: This sentence vents frustration that the counselors are always catching people at inopportune times and ignoring explanations to make their own judgments.
